x: MacIver and Page name two bases of a community: locality (a definite geographic territory) and community sentiment (we-feeling, a sense of solidarity) – option D. Option A is MacIver's definition ('sharing the basic conditions of a common life'), not its features. A sociology question, moved to book 2 row 105.
source: MacIver & Page, Society: An Introductory Analysis (1949), ch. Community (summarised at sociology.institute/?p=245444)
evidence: MacIver, Community: A Sociological Study (1917), archive.org
not in the NextGen / Rocket Indian Society files (src/society)
dispute: The printed key is A (MacIver's definition: a group sharing the basic conditions of a common life). Strictly the "bases" of community in MacIver & Page are locality and community sentiment (D).
